rule: Behavioural description. This is NOT a claim of sentence-exact correspondence with the code - the CODE is authoritative and this description is deliberately shorter than it. (1) SCOPE: every 64-hex string (case-insensitive) occurring in a file whose extension is .json (case-insensitive) is checked, whether it is a value under a dict key OR a bare element of a list. (2) TARGET SELECTION for a value under dict key K: if K ends with _sha256/_sha1/_sha/_hash/_digest, the NAME-AFFINE candidates are ALL present non-empty strings among {stem}_ref, {stem}_path, {stem}_file, {stem}_artifact, {stem}_artifact_ref, {stem}_locator, {stem} (stem = K without that suffix), and the authoritative key tuple is NOT consulted. Otherwise the candidates are ALL present non-empty strings among the PATHKEYS tuple - in that tuple's order, which is authoritative and is NOT restated here - plus K itself when K looks path-like (contains a slash, ends .json, or matches <hex>:<path>). (3) Of those candidates, the FIRST that RESOLVES is authoritative and must equal the value; later candidates are NOT examined. A candidate that does not resolve raises an error only when it is a relative path or a git reference AND no other candidate resolved. An absolute candidate whose basename is not uniquely in-tree is accepted when the value matches an in-tree or allowlisted blob. (4) If no candidate resolved - which is always the case for a bare list element, since it has no candidates - the value must equal the sha256 of some in-tree file or be in the external/historical allowlist. (5) Failures inside a superseded/ scope are collected in superseded_scope_stale_references rather than raised.
known_limitations: path-like strings that are not SELECTED targets are not examined: repo slugs such as 'shw097-team/SWOF', a descriptive 'locator' like 'branch X @ <sha>', and the original-key metadata field - these carry no byte claim

a declared value CAN be satisfied by allowlist membership (the historical commit's blobs, the out-of-tree contract, and named external control files) without the accompanying descriptive reference being independently verified

an ABSOLUTE path whose basename is not uniquely in-tree is accepted if the value matches an in-tree or allowlisted blob - the deliberate external-control-file allowance, and the clearest way a contradiction could still in principle be absorbed

when several targets are present only the FIRST that resolves is authoritative; a later path-like sibling that does not resolve is not additionally faulted. Consequence: an object carrying BOTH a path and an affine {stem}_ref is judged on the affine ref alone, so a contradictory path sibling is not caught
the allowlist is a minimal, enumerated external-reference set, not a general escape hatch
